As a person from the United States, I use both Imperial and Metric systems in everyday life and I'm comfortable with both. 

The only aspect of the metric system I find less appealing is its application to speed and distance. It's not that there's anything inherently wrong with it, but I find it less intuitive to calculate how long it will take to reach a destination 560 kilometers away while traveling at 80 kilometers per hour. I have these preset segments in my mind that help me estimate how long that kind of trip would take in miles per hour.

When I was driving through a country in North America a few years ago, I'd simply convert everything to imperial by looking down at my dash, as cars in the region have both mph and kph on the gauge cluster. It was somehow easier for me to convert everything to miles from meters, then I could figure out how long it would take me to get to my destination.

I realize this is wholly impractical, and rather counterintuitive, but it somehow works in my brain.

Also, that country is just as strange as another region when it comes to their measuring systems. Much of the time things were metric, but there were other times when it was both. "Yeah, so go down that highway for a few clicks, then you'll see this barn, so turn there and go down that road a few miles, where you'll see a lake a few miles off to your left, drive another few k, then you'll see the airport hanger on your right." "Fill up before you get there, as the price per gallon goes up the farther out you are." Fuel was sold by the liter, but at the airport, airplane fuel was sold in imperial gallons!
It's always tomorrow in a country down under. That's gotta be weird.
